name: The Patriarchs (Avot)
dom: the three forefathers; covenant lineage
note: The three forefathers of Israel — Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — invoked together as the recipients of the covenant.

name: The Matriarchs (Imahot)
dom: the four foremothers; covenant lineage
note: The four foremothers of Israel — Sarah, Rebecca, Rachel, and Leah — mothers of the covenant line.

name: The Twelve Tribes of Israel
dom: the sons of Jacob; the tribal confederation
note: The confederation of tribes descended from the sons of Jacob, who together constituted the people of Israel.

name: The Judges of Israel
dom: charismatic deliverers; pre-monarchic leadership
note: The charismatic deliverers who led the tribes of Israel in the period before the monarchy.

name: The Kings of the United Monarchy
dom: the united monarchy; Saul, David, Solomon
note: The three successive kings of the united Israelite kingdom — Saul, David, and Solomon — before its division.

name: Eve
dom: first woman; mother of humanity; the Fall
note: Formed as the first woman and 'mother of all living,' she eats the forbidden fruit and bears Cain, Abel, and Seth.

name: Cain
dom: firstborn of humanity; agriculture; fratricide
note: Firstborn son of Adam and Eve, a tiller of the ground who murdered his brother Abel and was marked and exiled.

name: Abel
dom: shepherding; accepted sacrifice; the first death
note: Second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of sheep whose offering was favored and who was slain by his brother Cain.

name: Seth
dom: third son of Adam; the righteous line to Noah
note: Third son of Adam and Eve, given in place of slain Abel, through whose line Enosh, Enoch, and Noah descend.

name: Abraham
dom: covenant; faith; the binding of Isaac; father of nations
note: First of the patriarchs, called from Ur, recipient of the covenant, father of Ishmael by Hagar and Isaac by Sarah.

name: Sarah
dom: matriarch; the promised son; the covenant line
note: Wife of Abraham and first matriarch, who bore Isaac in old age after the promise of a son.

name: Hagar
dom: the wilderness; divine encounter; mother of Ishmael
note: Egyptian servant of Sarah who bore Abraham's son Ishmael and was met by the angel of Yahweh in the wilderness.

name: Ishmael
dom: firstborn of Abraham; wilderness; ancestor of twelve princes
note: Firstborn son of Abraham by Hagar, ancestor of twelve princes, who dwelt in the wilderness of Paran.

name: Lot
dom: Sodom and Gomorrah; rescue from destruction
note: Nephew of Abraham (son of Haran) who settled in Sodom and was delivered from its destruction (Genesis 13, 19).

name: Isaac
dom: the promised son; the Akedah; covenant continuity
note: Son of Abraham and Sarah, bound on Mount Moriah, husband of Rebecca, and father of Esau and Jacob.

name: Rebecca
dom: matriarch; the well; mother of Jacob and Esau
note: Wife of Isaac, found at the well, mother of twins Esau and Jacob whom she helped secure the blessing.

name: Jacob (Israel)
dom: the ladder vision; wrestling the angel; father of the twelve tribes
note: Son of Isaac and Rebecca, renamed Israel after wrestling at Peniel, father of the twelve sons who became the tribes of Israel.

name: Rachel
dom: the beloved wife; mother of Joseph and Benjamin
note: Beloved wife of Jacob, mother of Joseph and Benjamin, who died in childbirth near Bethlehem.

name: Leah
dom: matriarch; mother of six tribes incl. Levi and Judah
note: First wife of Jacob and mother of six of his sons, including Levi and Judah, ancestors of priesthood and kingship.

name: Joseph (son of Jacob)
dom: dreams; bondage and exaltation; provision in famine
note: Favored son of Jacob and Rachel, sold into Egypt, who rose to vizier and preserved his family during famine.

name: Judah
cat: Eponym of the tribe of Judah
dom: tribal ancestor; the royal line; the scepter blessing
note: Fourth son of Jacob and Leah and ancestor of the royal Davidic line, blessed that the scepter would not depart.

name: Levi
dom: tribal ancestor; the priestly line
note: Third son of Jacob and Leah and ancestor of the priestly tribe of Levi, including Moses and Aaron.

name: Benjamin
cat: Eponym of the tribe of Benjamin
dom: youngest son of Jacob; tribal ancestor
note: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, born at her death, ancestor of the tribe of Benjamin and of King Saul.

name: Aaron
dom: the priesthood; spokesman of Moses; the golden calf
note: Brother of Moses and Miriam, spokesman before Pharaoh, and the first high priest of Israel.

name: Miriam
dom: prophecy; the song at the sea; leadership of the women
note: Sister of Moses and Aaron, called a prophetess, who led the women in song after the crossing of the sea.

name: Joshua
dom: conquest of Canaan; warfare; covenant renewal
note: Successor of Moses who led Israel across the Jordan and in the conquest of Canaan, dividing the land among the tribes.

name: Caleb
dom: faithful scouting; inheritance of Hebron; wholehearted devotion
note: One of the twelve spies who, with Joshua, trusted in Yahweh and was rewarded with the inheritance of Hebron.

name: Deborah
dom: prophecy; judgeship; the victory over Sisera
note: Prophetess and judge who summoned Barak and celebrated the defeat of Sisera in the Song of Deborah.

name: Gideon
dom: deliverance from Midian; the fleece sign; the three hundred
note: Judge who, with three hundred men, delivered Israel from the Midianites after testing Yahweh with the fleece.

name: Samson
dom: superhuman strength; the Nazirite vow; war with the Philistines
note: Nazirite judge of immense strength who fought the Philistines and died bringing down their temple at Gaza.

name: Samuel
dom: prophecy; judgeship; anointing of Saul and David
note: Last judge and a prophet who anointed both Saul and David as kings of Israel.

name: Saul
dom: the first monarchy; rejected kingship; war with the Philistines
note: First king of Israel from the tribe of Benjamin, anointed by Samuel, rejected for disobedience, and slain at Gilboa.

name: David
dom: kingship; the Davidic covenant; psalmody; warfare
note: Shepherd anointed by Samuel who slew Goliath, became king over all Israel, and received the everlasting dynastic covenant.

name: Bathsheba
dom: the royal household; mother of Solomon
note: Wife of David, taken after the death of Uriah, and mother of King Solomon.

name: Ruth
dom: loyalty (hesed); the gleaning; redemption; ancestress of David
note: Moabite widow whose loyalty to Naomi led to her marriage to Boaz, making her great-grandmother of King David.

name: Esther
cat: Queen of Persia / deliverer of the Jews
dom: deliverance of her people; the feast of Purim; courage
note: Jewish queen of Persia who risked her life before Ahasuerus to save her people, commemorated at Purim.

name: Mordecai
dom: the foiling of Haman; the institution of Purim
note: Kinsman and guardian of Esther who uncovered a plot, refused homage to Haman, and helped establish Purim.

name: Job
dom: undeserved suffering; perseverance; the divine speeches
note: A blameless man of Uz whose endurance of catastrophic suffering frames the book's debate on divine justice.

name: Ezra
dom: the Torah; restoration of the law; communal reform
note: Priest and scribe who led returning exiles and re-established the Torah in restored Jerusalem.

name: Nehemiah
dom: rebuilding Jerusalem's walls; civic reform; covenant renewal
note: Cupbearer to the Persian king who became governor and rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem and reformed the community.

name: The Latter Prophets (Nevi'im Aharonim)
dom: prophecy; covenant judgment and restoration; messianic hope
note: The prophetic canon division comprising the three Major Prophets and the Book of the Twelve, spanning the Assyrian, Babylonian, and Persian periods.

name: The Twelve Minor Prophets (Trei Asar)
dom: prophecy; social justice; the Day of the Lord; restoration
note: A single scroll in the Hebrew canon gathering twelve shorter prophetic books from the 8th century BCE to the post-exilic restoration.

name: Isaiah
dom: judgment; messianic hope; the suffering servant; the holiness of God
note: An 8th-century BCE Judahite prophet whose oracles warn of judgment yet promise a remnant, a Davidic messiah, and a restored Zion.

name: Jeremiah
dom: judgment; lament; the new covenant; faithfulness in exile
note: A late 7th- to early 6th-century BCE prophet who foretold Jerusalem's fall to Babylon and proclaimed a coming new covenant written on the heart.

name: Ezekiel
dom: exilic visions; divine glory; judgment and restoration
note: A 6th-century BCE priest-prophet among the Babylonian exiles whose visions of the chariot, dry bones, and a restored temple promise renewal.

name: Daniel
dom: apocalyptic vision; divine sovereignty over empires; eschatology
note: A Judahite exile at the Babylonian and Persian courts whose faithfulness and apocalyptic visions affirm God's rule over the kingdoms of the world.

name: Hosea
dom: covenant love; Israel's unfaithfulness; divine mercy
note: An 8th-century BCE prophet to the northern kingdom whose troubled marriage dramatizes Israel's faithlessness and God's enduring covenant love.

name: Joel
dom: the Day of the Lord; locust plague; outpouring of the Spirit
note: A prophet of Judah who reads a devastating locust plague as a sign of the coming Day of the Lord and promises an outpouring of God's Spirit.

name: Amos
dom: social justice; judgment on the nations; righteousness over ritual
note: A mid-8th-century BCE Judahite shepherd who prophesied against the northern kingdom, condemning injustice and empty worship.

name: Obadiah
dom: judgment on Edom; vindication of Zion; the Day of the Lord
note: Author of the shortest book of the Hebrew Bible, an oracle of judgment against Edom for its betrayal of Judah.

name: Jonah
dom: divine mercy to the nations; reluctant prophecy; repentance
note: A reluctant prophet, swallowed by a great fish, whose mission to Nineveh reveals God's compassion even toward Israel's enemies.

name: Micah
dom: social justice; judgment on Samaria and Jerusalem; the Bethlehem ruler
note: An 8th-century BCE contemporary of Isaiah who called Israel to do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.

name: Nahum
dom: judgment on Nineveh; divine vengeance; comfort for Judah
note: A 7th-century BCE prophet who proclaimed the impending fall of Nineveh as God's judgment on a cruel empire.

name: Habakkuk
dom: theodicy; faith amid injustice; 'the righteous shall live by faith'
note: A late 7th-century BCE prophet who questioned God about the Babylonian threat and concluded that the righteous shall live by their faith.

name: Zephaniah
dom: the Day of the Lord; universal judgment; the humble remnant
note: A 7th-century BCE Judahite prophet during Josiah's reign who warned of a sweeping Day of the Lord and promised salvation for a humble remnant.

name: Haggai
dom: rebuilding the temple; post-exilic restoration; priorities of worship
note: A post-exilic prophet of 520 BCE who urged the returned exiles to rebuild the Jerusalem temple and promised future glory.

name: Zechariah
dom: apocalyptic visions; temple restoration; messianic hope
note: A post-exilic prophet, contemporary of Haggai, whose night visions encouraged the temple's rebuilding and foretold a coming messianic king.

name: Malachi
dom: covenant fidelity; corrupt priesthood; the coming messenger
note: The last of the Twelve, a 5th-century BCE prophet who rebuked unfaithfulness and announced a coming messenger before the Day of the Lord.

name: Elisha
dom: prophetic succession; miracles; care for the lowly
note: A 9th-century BCE prophet of the northern kingdom who succeeded Elijah, receiving a double portion of his spirit and performing many miracles.

name: Nathan
dom: court prophecy; the Davidic covenant; royal accountability
note: A 10th-century BCE court prophet under King David who delivered the Davidic covenant promise and rebuked David over Bathsheba and Uriah.

name: The Twelve Apostles
dom: the twelve disciples chosen by Jesus; foundation of the Church
note: The twelve disciples chosen by Jesus as his closest followers and witnesses, the foundation of the apostolic Church.

name: The Four Evangelists
dom: the authors of the four canonical Gospels
note: Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John — the traditional authors of the four canonical Gospels.

name: The Pauline Circle
dom: companions and coworkers of the apostle Paul
note: The missionary companions and coworkers of the apostle Paul named in Acts and the epistles — Barnabas, Mark, Luke, Timothy, and Titus.

name: Andrew
dom: first-called apostle; brother of Peter; the saltire cross
note: A fisherman of Bethsaida and brother of Simon Peter, called by Jesus to be a fisher of men and numbered among the Twelve.

name: John, son of Zebedee
dom: the beloved disciple; the Fourth Gospel; Revelation
note: Son of Zebedee and brother of James the Greater, traditionally identified with the Beloved Disciple and reckoned both apostle and evangelist.

name: Philip
dom: apostle of Bethsaida; bringer of Nathanael; questioner at the Supper
note: A native of Bethsaida who, on being called by Jesus, sought out Nathanael with the words 'Come and see.'

name: Bartholomew (Nathanael)
dom: apostle; 'an Israelite without guile'; identified with Nathanael
note: Listed among the Twelve as Bartholomew and commonly identified with the Nathanael whom Jesus praised as guileless in John's Gospel.

name: Thomas
dom: doubt and confession; called Didymus; 'My Lord and my God'
note: An apostle called Didymus who doubted the resurrection until he saw the risen Christ, then confessed him as 'My Lord and my God.'

name: Matthew (Levi)
dom: tax collector called by Jesus; the First Gospel
note: A tax collector (the Levi of Mark and Luke) called by Jesus, numbered among the Twelve and traditionally credited with the First Gospel.

name: James, son of Alphaeus
dom: apostle of the Twelve; 'James the Less'
note: An apostle named in all four lists of the Twelve as the son of Alphaeus, distinct from James the son of Zebedee.

name: Jude (Thaddaeus)
dom: apostle; Thaddaeus / 'Judas of James'
note: An apostle listed as Thaddaeus in Matthew and Mark and as Judas son (or brother) of James in Luke and Acts.

name: Simon the Zealot
dom: apostle; the Zealot / the Cananaean
note: An apostle of the Twelve called the Zealot (or Cananaean) to distinguish him from Simon Peter.

name: Judas Iscariot
dom: betrayal; keeper of the money bag; thirty pieces of silver
note: The apostle who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver and afterward died, his place among the Twelve filled by Matthias.

name: Matthias
dom: apostle chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot
note: A disciple who had followed Jesus from his baptism and was chosen by lot to take the place of Judas Iscariot among the Twelve.

name: Mark
dom: evangelist; the Second Gospel; companion of Paul, Barnabas, Peter
note: John Mark, a companion of Paul, Barnabas, and Peter, traditionally identified as the author of the Second Gospel.

name: Luke
dom: evangelist and physician; the Third Gospel and Acts; companion of Paul
note: A physician and companion of Paul, traditionally credited with the Third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles.

name: Barnabas
dom: 'son of encouragement'; missionary companion of Paul
note: A Levite of Cyprus surnamed Barnabas ('son of encouragement') who introduced Paul to the apostles and traveled with him as a missionary.

name: Timothy
dom: Paul's coworker and delegate; leader at Ephesus
note: A disciple of Lystra, son of a Jewish mother and Greek father, who became Paul's close coworker and the recipient of two epistles.

name: Titus
dom: Paul's Greek coworker; envoy to Corinth; organizer in Crete
note: A Greek coworker of Paul, sent to Corinth and left in Crete to set its churches in order, and the recipient of the Epistle to Titus.

name: Lazarus of Bethany
dom: raised from the dead by Jesus; brother of Martha and Mary
note: The brother of Martha and Mary of Bethany, whom Jesus raised from the dead after four days in the tomb.

name: Martha
dom: hostess of Jesus at Bethany; confessor of Christ
note: A sister of Lazarus and Mary who served Jesus at Bethany and confessed him as the Christ, the Son of God.

name: Nicodemus
dom: Pharisee who came to Jesus by night; helped bury Jesus
note: A Pharisee and member of the Sanhedrin who came to Jesus by night and later helped Joseph of Arimathea bury him.

name: The Prophets of Islam (Anbiya)
dom: the line of prophets and messengers; revelation; pure monotheism (tawhid)
note: The collective of prophets named in the Qur'an, from Adam to Muhammad, sent to guide humanity to the worship of the one God.

name: Ulu al-Azm
dom: the five arch-prophets of firm resolve, each bringing a major scripture/law
note: Ulu al-Azm ('those of firm resolve') are the five greatest messengers in Islam: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad.

name: Adam (Islam)
dom: the first human and first prophet; God's vicegerent (khalifa); the names of all things
note: Adam, the first man and first prophet in Islam, created by God and taught the names of all things; the Islamic reception of the Biblical Adam.

name: Nuh
dom: the Ark and the Flood; persistent call to monotheism; Ulu al-Azm
note: Nuh built the Ark at God's command and was saved with the believers from the Flood; the Islamic reception of Noah.

name: Hud
dom: prophet to the people of 'Ad; warning against idolatry and arrogance
note: Hud was sent to the ancient Arabian people of 'Ad to call them from idolatry; an Arabian prophet with no Biblical counterpart.

name: Salih
dom: prophet to Thamud; the miraculous she-camel
note: Salih was sent to the Arabian people of Thamud with the sign of the she-camel; an Arabian prophet with no Biblical counterpart.

name: Ibrahim
dom: khalil Allah (friend of God); the Kaaba; pure monotheism (hanif); Ulu al-Azm
note: Ibrahim, the friend of God, patriarch of monotheism who with his son built the Kaaba; the Islamic reception of Abraham.

name: Lut
dom: prophet to the cities of the plain; warning against immorality
note: Lut warned his people against immorality before their destruction; the Islamic reception of Lot.

name: Ismail
dom: son of Ibrahim; the son of the sacrifice; co-builder of the Kaaba; ancestor of the Arabs
note: Ismail, son of Ibrahim, helped build the Kaaba and is regarded in Islam as the son offered in sacrifice; the Islamic reception of Ishmael.

name: Ishaq
dom: son of Ibrahim; patriarch of the Israelite prophets
note: Ishaq, son of Ibrahim, was given to him in old age and continued the prophetic line; the Islamic reception of Isaac.

name: Yaqub
dom: son of Ishaq; also called Israil; patriarch of the twelve tribes
note: Yaqub (Israil), son of Ishaq and father of Yusuf, was a prophet and patriarch; the Islamic reception of Jacob.

name: Yusuf
dom: interpreter of dreams; betrayal and rise in Egypt; chastity and forgiveness
note: Yusuf, son of Yaqub, was sold into Egypt and rose to power, subject of the Qur'an's 'most beautiful story'; the Islamic reception of Joseph.

name: Ayyub
dom: patience (sabr) under affliction; restoration by God
note: Ayyub endured severe affliction with patience and was restored by God, an exemplar of sabr; the Islamic reception of Job.

name: Shu'ayb
dom: prophet to Madyan; honest weights and measures; monotheism
note: Shu'ayb was sent to the people of Madyan to enjoin honest dealing and monotheism; an Arabian prophet often linked, but not equated, with Jethro.

name: Musa
dom: kalim Allah (the one God spoke to); the Exodus; the Tawrah; Ulu al-Azm
note: Musa, the one to whom God spoke directly, led the Israelites from Egypt and received the Tawrah; the Islamic reception of Moses.

name: Harun
dom: brother and helper (wazir) of Musa; spokesman before Pharaoh
note: Harun was the brother of Musa and his appointed helper and spokesman; the Islamic reception of Aaron.

name: Dhul-Kifl
dom: patience and steadfastness; often identified with Ezekiel
note: Dhul-Kifl is a patient prophet named among the righteous, commonly identified by Muslim tradition with Ezekiel.

name: Dawud
dom: prophet-king; slayer of Jalut (Goliath); the Zabur (Psalms); judgment and song
note: Dawud, the prophet-king who slew Jalut and received the Zabur, was given a beautiful voice and wisdom in judgment; the Islamic reception of David.

name: Sulayman
dom: prophet-king; command of wind, jinn, and animals; the Queen of Sheba
note: Sulayman, son of Dawud, was a prophet-king granted command over wind and jinn and knowledge of the speech of animals; the Islamic reception of Solomon.

name: Ilyas
dom: opposition to the worship of Baal; call to the one God
note: Ilyas called his people away from the worship of Baal to the one God; the Islamic reception of Elijah.

name: Al-Yasa
dom: prophet among the righteous; successor in the line of Ilyas
note: Al-Yasa is named among the excellent prophets and follows in the line of Ilyas; the Islamic reception of Elisha.

name: Yunus
dom: the prophet of the fish (Dhul-Nun); repentance; mission to Nineveh
note: Yunus, also called Dhul-Nun, was swallowed by a great fish and delivered after repenting, then sent to a people who believed; the Islamic reception of Jonah.

name: Zakariya
dom: guardian of Maryam; granted a son (Yahya) in old age
note: Zakariya was guardian of Maryam and was granted the son Yahya in old age; counterpart of the New Testament Zechariah, father of John the Baptist.

name: Yahya
dom: son of Zakariya; wisdom in youth; righteousness and chastity
note: Yahya, son of Zakariya, was given wisdom as a child and was pure and devout; the Islamic reception of John the Baptist.

name: Isa
dom: al-Masih (the Messiah); born of Maryam; the Injil; miracles by God's leave; Ulu al-Azm
note: Isa al-Masih, son of Maryam, was born of a virgin, given the Injil, and worked miracles by God's leave, regarded in Islam as prophet and not divine; the Islamic reception of Jesus.

name: Luqman
dom: the sage granted wisdom (hikma); moral counsel to his son
note: Luqman is a wise man granted hikma by God who gives moral counsel to his son; revered as a sage (and by some a prophet), with no Biblical counterpart.
